1. Core Clinical Tension: A 48-year-old rural laborer with no tobacco history or chronic comorbidities presents with a single large, 4 cm bleeding oral ulcer. Even without smoking history, an aggressive 4 cm bleeding ulcer must be distinguished from oral squamous cell carcinoma or reactive vascular lesions.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage terminates after inspection of the 4 cm bleeding ulcer with hemorrhagic dots, strictly prior to obtaining tissue for anatomopathological examination.
3. Differential Distinctions: Squamous cell carcinoma generally exhibits hard, everted margins with central necrosis, whereas paracoccidioidomycosis manifests as a granulomatous ulcer with fine punctate hemorrhages ('moriform' appearance). Pyogenic granuloma and traumatic ulcerative granuloma present as reactive vascular or ulcerated masses, but lack the diffuse fungal granulomatous infiltration seen on biopsy.
case_prompt: A 48-year-old male rural worker with no history of tobacco use, substance use, or chronic medical comorbidities presents to the clinic with a chief complaint of a "bleeding wound in the mouth." Physical examination of the oral cavity reveals an ulcerated lesion measuring approximately 4 cm associated with hemorrhagic dots.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A solitary, large (4 cm) bleeding oral ulcer in an adult male warrants high clinical suspicion for oral malignancy; however, anatomopathological evaluation showed infectious fungal features rather than malignancy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: PMC was confirmed after anatomopathological examination.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Traumatic / Vascular Ulcerative Lesion (e.g., Pyogenic Granuloma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The sudden complaint of a bleeding wound in a healthy manual worker suggested an acute traumatic or reactive vascular mucosal process, but examination showed a classic 4 cm ulcer with fine hemorrhagic dots characteristic of a deep mycotic infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Clinical examination revealed an ulcer lesion of approximately 4 cm associated with hemorrhagic dots (Figure 10).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Anatomopathological examination of the 4 cm bleeding ulcer established the definitive diagnosis, leading to prompt therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: PMC was confirmed after anatomopathological examination. Therapy started promptly with trimethoprim + sulfamethoxazole.

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint strictly observed. Case prompt is devoid of pathogen names and biopsy findings. Quotes are exact verbatim text from the published report.
